# CARL revision-denominator ledger (answers RED's 9/14 ask)

**Status:** DRAFT v0, 2026-09-24 eve. Not yet delivered to RED (due 2026-09-30).
**Ask (RED, 9/14):** *"Every CRL revision since registration, with direction-of-benefit and magnitude … Name the denominator before any shape word."*
**Data:** `thesis/REVISION_LEDGER.tsv`, 120 events, one row each. Generated by `scripts/revision_ledger.py --classify` from the full git history of `thesis/PREDICTIONS.tsv` (62 commits, 2026-03-04 → 2026-09-11, 204 days, 30 predictions). Rerun it to reproduce. The hand judgements sit in `OVERRIDES` in that script, and **they are the part to attack.**

---

## 1 · Answer first

| Measure | Figure |
|---|---|
| Revision decisions (registrations, resolutions and annotations excluded) | **61** in 204 days (~2.1/week) |
| of which confidence reprices | 42 |
| of which structural (window, re-spec, disposition, record correction) | 19 |
| Reprices by thesis direction | **29 cuts (−589pp) vs 13 raises (+93pp).** The stream runs heavily AGAINST the bear thesis |
| Reprices toward the eventual outcome (final-mark benefit) | 27 of 35 determinable (9 of 10 on resolved rows; the rest PROVISIONAL) |
| Structural, **CARL-initiated** (incl. Will-approved) | **13: 10 HELPED CARL's record, 1 hurt, 1 depends on convention, 1 undetermined** |
| Structural, **forced by an outside audit** (POLLY, DAEDALUS) | **6: all 6 HURT** |

**The reading RED asked for:** the reprice stream is not self-serving on either count. It mostly cuts CARL's own thesis, and under as-made scoring a reprice cannot move the Brier at all. **The structural stream is where the signal is, and it leans the way RED first worried:** when CARL used its own discretion on a window, spec or disposition, 10 of 13 calls helped its record. Every revision that hurt was forced from outside, or was CARL's own audit rule (the CRL-07 "force a call, do not roll again").

⚠️ **RED's counterexample needs re-grading, and so does CARL's 9/10 claim built on it.** See §4.

---

## 2 · Method and conventions

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| REPRICE | leading confidence number changed on a live row |
| WINDOW | resolution window materially moved (extension or hard close). Date typos and notes are ANNOTATION |
| RESPEC | the claim's threshold or legs changed |
| DISPOSITION | a discretionary status call: CONFIRMED*, MIXED, RETIRED, NO-VERDICT, re-scoped to a pointer |
| RECORD-CORRECTION | a re-mark of the record itself (the 9/10 DAEDALUS H2 as-made re-marks) |
| thesis_dir | FOR = raises bear confidence, extends or keeps a row alive; AGAINST = the reverse |
| benefit_final | effect on CARL's scored record if rows score at the **final mark** |
| benefit_asmade | effect if rows score at the **as-made** confidence. Reprices are then NEUTRAL by construction |
| Outcome basis | resolved Status. For OPEN rows, CARL's current confidence: ≤25% = likely MISS, ≥75% = likely HIT, else UNDETERMINED. Tagged `PROV` |

⚠️ **"Helps the record" is not evidence of bias by itself.** A reprice toward the eventual outcome is what honest updating looks like. The bias test is the **discretionary structural set**, where the choice was not forced by a print.

## 4 · Two corrections this ledger forces

### 4a · CRL-05 counts as "hurt" only under final-mark scoring
RED's 9/14 packet treated the CRL-05 void as the case that already falsifies "CARL revises when it helps", and CARL's own 9/10 CHANGELOG says so too: *"THE VOID COSTS ME A GOOD SCORE."* That is true **only at the final mark** (20% → a MISS scores 0.04). **At the as-made mark (75%), a MISS scores 0.5625, and the void removes it.** CARL used the final-mark convention on CRL-05 **on the same day it re-marked CRL-03/04/06/11 to as-made.** One convention cannot be used for the rows that hurt and the other for the row that helps. **Under CARL's own post-9/10 convention, the CRL-05 void HELPED.**

### 4b · The resolved rows are scored on two conventions at once
| Row | Outcome | Published mark | As-made | Brier published → as-made |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CRL-03 / 04 / 06 / 11 | MIS / CON / CON / MIS | as-made (re-marked 9/10) | same | — |
| **CRL-07** | MISSED | **40%** ("FINAL MARK AT RESOLUTION") | 80% (3/09) | 0.16 → **0.64** |
| **CRL-16** | MISSED | **35%** | 60% (4/10) | 0.1225 → **0.36** |
| CRL-09 | MISSED | 73% | 75% (3/31) | 0.5329 → 0.5625 |

**The two MISSED rows still published at walked-down marks are exactly where a final-mark convention flatters most: +0.72 Brier combined if re-marked.** CARL does **not** recompute the aggregate here, because the scoreboard belongs to the DAEDALUS ladder. **A convention ruling is owed, and it cuts both ways:** as-made re-marks CRL-07/16 upward (worse) **and** turns the CRL-05 void into a help.

## 6 · Limits (read before quoting any figure above)
1. **PROV outcomes** rest on CARL's own current confidence. 18 of the 27 helping reprices are PROV.
2. **Only the TSV is seen.** Confidence moves made in STATUS before the TSV caught up (the 5/22 CRL-05 reprice reached the TSV 6/8) are dated at the TSV commit. Two edits inside one commit collapse into one.
3. **The TSV's IDs are claim-consistent.** Checked at `9e30a573c` and `bf073316a`: the early ID reassignment in the as-made audit affected STATUS, not the TSV.
4. **Magnitude:** reprices in pp. Structural rows carry Brier stakes where computable (§3 notes, §4b). Windows carry time added: CRL-08 went from Apr 5 to Sep 30, ~178 days.
5. **Will approved** CRL-14 retirement, CRL-22 v2 and v3. Approval is recorded, and it does not change the benefit direction.
6. **Sub-agent ledgers** (PHAN/POP/DOC/POLLY/GIG, 23 OPEN rows) are **not** in scope. RED asked for CRL rows.

**Before delivery:** a hostile read of the 19 OVERRIDES rows, since those are the hand-judged part.
